I’ll add to what you’ve said: under Stalin, Moscow was rebuilt on a large scale, and not just through the construction of skyscrapers — primarily through the reorganization and expansion of the city’s streets. In 1935, the Moscow government approved the resolution “On the General Plan for the Reconstruction of the City of Moscow.” The master plan was developed under the leadership of architects Vladimir Semyonov and Sergei Chernyshev and envisaged the creation of new wide transport thoroughfares and the expansion of existing ones, the construction of bridges, the building of the metro, and the water supply and landscaping of Moscow. A huge number of buildings were moved using jacks, without relocating the residents.
By the way, a clarification regarding St. Petersburg. It wasn’t a territory seized from the Swedes, but a liberated one, since it was the Swedes who seized this territory from the Novgorod Republic.
